## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
- The `test_setup` risco sensor platform test is flaky.
- The problem seems to be that the sensor platform depends on the binary sensor entity state but when the sensor platform is set up and the sensor state is collected, the binary sensor may not be ready yet. The test doesn't take this into account although the production code handles this case with a check.


## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 2021.2.0.dev0
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): 
- Integration causing this issue: risco
- Link to integration documentation on our website:

<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

comments:
Hey there @onfreund, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`risco`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L375) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Thanks @MartinHjelmare. It always worked for me so I didn't notice. Is there a way to wait on the `binary_sensor` platform being loaded?

We could move time forward and let the state update again before asserting it.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2ed7b90027cb28b5f78f40257845475cc546da9c/tests/common.py#L286
Is it guaranteed that the binary sensors will be loaded before the second update?

We await the platforms (using `hass.async_block_till_done`) before asserting the state. That's not the problem, I think. The problem is that the state of the sensor platform is collected and set in the state machine before the binary sensor platform is done loading.

Got it. In that case shouldn't switching the order of lines 197 & 198 in the test solve this?
From:
```
await coordinator.async_refresh()
await hass.async_block_till_done()
```

to:
```
await hass.async_block_till_done()
await coordinator.async_refresh()
```

(I'm not sure how to reproduce so I can't really test that it fixes it)
(to clarify - there's no explicit call to `coordinator.async_refresh()` in the integration itself. This call should be the first)
We shouldn't use the coordinator at all in the test. We should just move time forward. The test shouldn't interact with integration details like the coordinator.

Ok, attempted fix at: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/44788
Since I can't reproduce, I have no way of testing this actually fixes the problem.

review_comments: I don't think we need to remove this. But we normally refresh the coordinator in the init module after creating it before loading platforms that need it so they already have data in the cache.

I wanted to avoid refreshing the coordinator before the binary sensor platform is ready.
I can move this to a `EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STARTED` listener if you think that's better than removing.
I don't think that is a problem. Why do you think that? I'd move the refresh before any platform is loaded.
Because if we refresh before the binary sensor platform is loaded, the `zone_entity_id` attribute is missing.
It will potentially be missing on the first sensor state update regardless since we don't control the order of platform load.
And I don't think this is a problem since we have a guard in the sensor platform for missing zone entity_id. It will populate on next refresh.

It won't populate on next refresh - the coordinator only fetches new events. I think that in this case delaying the value by 60 seconds (and unless HA was down for a long time, in most cases no event happened while HA was down, so there shouldn't be a value anyway) is better than having partial info forever.

Ok. If we want to refresh earlier we can await the platforms forwarding and refresh the coordinator after that. See an example of this pattern here:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f771d8ff142a98a47eb25adf726e8771bf2bf36a/homeassistant/components/ozw/__init__.py#L261-L296
when I try that the tests hang.
My bad. I got it working
